svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A transverse wave: each particle moves up and down while the wave travels to the right."], [2, "Watch the red particle in each wave: it stays near its own rest position. Energy moves along the wave; the particles do not."], [4, "A longitudinal wave: particles move back and forth along the direction of travel, making compressions and rarefactions."], [6, "Both waves have a wavelength, a frequency and an amplitude; wave speed = frequency \u00d7 wavelength (v = f \u03bb)."]]
svg.title: Transverse and longitudinal waves
svg.desc: A transverse wave with crest, trough, rest position, amplitude and wavelength, and a longitudinal wave with compressions, rarefactions and wavelength. Play: the waves travel to the right while marked particles only oscillate.
svg.text: Play: the waves travel to the right. The red particles only oscillate about their own positions.

g.data-info: Where each particle is when there is no wave.
Particles move at right angles (perpendicular) to the direction of energy transfer. Examples: light and all electromagnetic waves, ripples on water, S-waves.
It only oscillates about its own rest position: the wave carries energy, not the medium.
Maximum displacement of a particle from its rest position (rest to crest). A bigger amplitude carries more energy (louder sound, brighter light).
Distance from one point on a wave to the same point on the next wave: crest to crest, or compression to compression.
The direction energy is transferred. Wave speed = frequency × wavelength (v = f λ).
Particles move back and forth parallel to the direction of energy transfer. Examples: sound, P-waves, a pushed slinky.
It only oscillates about its own rest position: the wave carries energy, not the medium.
Region where the particles are closest together (higher pressure).
Region where the particles are furthest apart (lower pressure).
Distance from one point on a wave to the same point on the next wave: crest to crest, or compression to compression.
